LESSON: READING 6.4.1 ORAL LITERATURE SONGS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 6
Topic 6.4: Reading 6.4.1 Oral literature Songs
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 6.4.1 Oral literature Songs, part of Strand 6 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How are songs similar to poems?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify repeated words and phrases in lullabies,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 6.4.1 Oral literature Songs in the Kenya CBC curriculum.

   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 6.4.1 Oral literature Songs in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. pick out key messages communicated in lullabies,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 6.4.1 Oral literature Songs in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 6.4.1 Oral literature Songs together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

 Critical thinking and problem solving is enhanced as the learner thinks of different ways of describing manner, time, and

place.

 Learning to learn is developed when the learner organises own learning as they identify and use different types of adverbs.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. identify repeated words and phrases in lullabies,
2. use appropriate techniques when performing lullabies,
3. pick out key messages communicated in lullabies,
4. appreciate the importance of lullabies in real life.  Listen to audio recordings of lullabies,  View videos of lullabies and identify instances of repetition. Learners with postural limitation could be preferentially positioned for enhanced viewing.  Perform a lullaby and make a recording.
